text:
Dubai registered 10,195 residential sales valued at AED 27,672,330,524 in the last four weeks, a 6.1 percent decrease from the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,054, recorded separately from sales. The off-plan share of transactions stood at 59.4 percent, down from 66.6 percent in the previous four weeks.

The median residential price per square foot declined 1.8 percent to AED 1,666. Top sales volumes in the last 12 weeks were led by Dubai South with 3,783 units at a median of AED 1,693 per square foot. Jumeirah Village Circle followed with 2,313 sales at AED 1,407 per square foot. Down Town Jabal Ali recorded 2,231 sales with a median price of AED 1,744 per square foot.

Rental activity included 92,517 Ejari contracts with a 50.2 percent renewal rate. The median residential rent was AED 70,000 annually. Estimated gross yields were highest in Zaabeel First at 9.1 percent for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent. Town Square posted a 6.9 percent yield, while Dubai Production City and Dubai Sports City both recorded yields above 6.5 percent.

Price momentum varied across communities. Al Yufrah 1 showed a 37.7 percent increase in median price per square foot over 12 weeks. In contrast, Liwan cooled by 14.0 percent and Palm Deira by 13.3 percent. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,076 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
